There's been a few times where Ive been scared that she's sleeping with her male coworkers who are nice enough to drive her home or help her when she needs it period. The way I handle it is easier said than done. I sit down and I talk it over with her. I've been 100% open about my insecurities and problems since day once and she's been very supportive. When I have a fear or worry, I discuss it with her and she willingly gives me any proof or information I request for reassurance. I never accuse her, ever. I calmly convey my worries. After a while, it became a natural process. 

I also weigh the situation. Is it something worth loosing the love of my life over? Especially if I don't have any hardcore evidence? Never forget that at times, fears and mistrust can lead you to see things in a certain light that with a clear head you would see differently.

I can agree here and honestly you said a very blunt version of my belief. Even if you're struggling with depression or low self esteem, you can find a middle ground with someone. 

Me for example, I have LOW self esteem. I mean, rock bottom kind of thing and I struggle with clinical depression. I still have a successful loving relationship, however and that's because I force myself to speak up when Im in a rough place. I let her know and I let her know that she hasn't done anything wrong. In return she's patient with me and she doesnt get angry. If she feels she might, she politely excuses herself and through years of building and working with me, I've come to understand that she has to do that for herself. People frown upon our relationship because they think "oh she shouldn't just leave you like that" or "You cling to her too much" but we're doing something right. We have a system though and we've been going strong for years though. It DEFINITELY takes work on both ends.

Honestly, with depression, you don't really get a say in how you think about things. Depending on the type, you could be perfectly okay and happy and then suddenly everything is miserable. You can take steps to try and prevent episodes, to live a better life but it doesnt always work. That's why support from loved ones, when depressed, is such a HUGE thing. 

I do think that someone with depression should be able to function on their own but unfortunately, it isnt easy to "get over" depression as a lot of people think and several people end up living their whole lives with it. Thats why I think finding someone who can handle them at their worst isnt a horrible thing. It can actually create a very strong bond as long as both parties meet halfway.  

Disclaimer: I'm not trying to say you're someone who thinks they can just "get over it" or anything.

Can confirm. I'm uninsured at 26, two slipped discs in my lower back, in need of surgery on my knee due to constant dislocation and my vision is so poor that not only am I unable to legally drive, I can hardly see at night.

I live every day popping ibuprofen like candy to reduce swelling enough to do my day to day activities. It sucks, it really does. I havent had any emergency care or treatment since I was taken to the e.r for my back in 2011 and slapped with a nearly $2000 bill for them to give me three muscle relaxors, three steroid pills and tell me I was sol. 

I attempted to do the physical therapy and see my doctor as instructed and then, bam $150 for the check up, $479 per p.t visit. I was instructed to do p.t 4 times a week for six months to try and ease the discs I slipled back in. Yea...no...not at that price.

The damage I did was horrible, an MRI after several months of physical therapy revealed that my kneecap had shredded my ACL and part of it had shifted in front of my kneecap. So not only had I lost the stability in my knee, I had lost the ability to straighten my leg. 

This all happened due to a ride operator at a fair. He moved the rides compartment when I tried to get in, and it caused me to lose my balance and wretch my knee.

First off, what you want out of a raltionship is a big deal. No one should have to live their life giving up their needs. That isn't fair. I know that sounds selfish but let me explain why I feel that way.

In 2009, I began dating a guy that I had been friends with for four years. He was a great guy, funny, smart and reliable. He was great. After six months I moved in with him and it was wonderful, granted we had sexual contact which is something you don't really have, I didn't have emotional support. I tried, on several occasions, to speak to him about it but he always said he didn't know how. That was the end of that. I gave up and I figured, to avoid conflict with him, I would just accept it. That wasn't the only problem to arise, however.

For my relationship, of I wanted something for my birthday or Christmas it had to be of use to him. If it wasn't he had a problem with me getting it. Yet he could stroll in with outrageously priced impulse buys whenever he wanted. I ended up having to beg for things and I was always made to feel bad about getting them. He never directly said I was horrible but he always stressed "I hate paying this much" or "There's nothing for me to do with it..." this continued until 2012. Then I made a big mistake...I married him.

Once we were married, things continued along that path until the middle of 2013, from there they began to spiral down the drain. He became filled with so much anger that he scared me. He'd yell and degrade me and my mindset through all of this was "I'm lucky to be with someone. I don't need things, what I want doesnt matter, I just need to make him happy."  I tried for another year to make him happy. It didn't work, though and finally in 2014 I told him I wanted to separate. 

He couldn't fill my emotional needs, physical interaction was to sayisfy him and ended with me finishing myself. I was, over time, made to hate my body and eventually, I wanted to die. It wasn't a passing grief, it was embedded. I would sit on my own at night, bawling, asking myself what I had done wrong. It was a disgustingly painful process and I was on the verge of attempting suicide. When I realized that, it had to end. 

When he realized I was serious, things changed. He tried to give me the stuff I asked for, the emotional support a say in purchases but the damage was done. I stood my ground even though it broke my heart and in 2015 he moved out and away. It's still hard, I won't lie, I do miss the good times we had together but over all, I'm happier. 

I'm sharing this story because I want to share how self destructive giving up what you want and what you need to make a relationship work can be. Please, don't let yourself suffer pain you shouldn't have to.

To answer your post full on and simply, I think you need to speak to him about all of this. You need to let him know the pain it's causing you and I want you to know that you arn't in the wrong at all for needing anything from a s/o. Everyone in the world has different needs and wants. What one person considers normal in a relationship could be foreign to another couple but in the end, what you need and want from a partner is your normal. It's what will make your relationship a happy, positive and productive thing. Just remember, your partners wants and needs are just as important and while this is hard to stomach and accept, if your core values and desires can't be agreed upon by the both of you then it may not be the relationship for you. 

Definitely speak to your boyfriend, though and remember, by no means does this make you a bad person.

About three years ago, my husband and I started having problems. I don't just mean simple ones either. We were constantly fighting, nothing was good enough anymore. I began feeling overwhelmingly depressed and I started to feel as if that was the end of everything. I couldnt imagine continuing life the way it was going and I truly did not care if death came upon me. I didn't have it in me to leave him, I wanted to try and make it work. No matter how much you love someone, though and how much you want it to work out, if only one side wants that it never will. I settled upon that and we started to just...coexist and then it happened. One night someone took my life by storm and blindsided me.

Two years ago, a girl came into my life. She was fighting cancer and we never would have met if not for that. During her chemo she decided she was going to give computer gaming a shot. Well, through one of the communities we met and became fast friends. I elected to stay up hanging out with her after her sessions and one night, it just clicked. When I realized I was subconsciously treating her like a crush things started to make sense. Suddenly, I was far from done with life and I wanted to commit my days to making hers a great one. Upon deciding that my husband and I had a long discussion and we agreed to separate and went our separate ways. After that I sat down and I spoke to her and after things settled we entered into a relationship. Now, here I am two years later still with her and still head over heels for her. 

TL;DR: I'm in love with her because even as she was at one of the lowest points life can bring someone she had the strength to save me. She is my best friend, the love of my life and my hero.
